tier_reason: Independent third-party shootout (djkoloski/rust_serialization_benchmark, code in benches/bench.rs + src/) whose README states rustc 1.100.0-nightly (a36d05efa 2026-09-09)/LLVM 23.1.1 and AMD EPYC 9V74. Cargo.toml [profile.bench] sets lto = true, so the flags are stated. savefile 0.20.5 and prost 0.14.4 (protobuf) rows both appear with the quoted numbers.

corrections.claimed_speedup: rust_serialization_benchmark README (last updated 2026-09-10), savefile 0.20.5 vs protobuf/prost 0.14.4. log: serialize 154.62 us vs prost encode 731.23 us (~4.7x) or populate+encode 1.8883 ms (~12.2x); deserialize 1.6639 ms vs prost decode 2.6802 ms (~1.6x). mesh: serialize 142.33 us vs prost encode 5.8939 ms (~41x) or populate+encode 6.3456 ms (~44.6x); deserialize 142.38 us vs prost decode 10.253 ms (~72x). minecraft_savedata: serialize 135.67 us vs encode 1.0006 ms (~7.4x); deserialize 1.5679 ms vs decode 2.6936 ms (~1.7x). mk48: serialize 581.79 us vs encode 4.5619 ms (~7.8x); deserialize 2.3372 ms vs decode 6.7080 ms (~2.9x). All ratios derived from page data.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: rustc 1.100.0-nightly (a36d05efa 2026-09-09), LLVM 23.1.1; cargo bench (Criterion) with [profile.bench] lto = true (release opt-level)
corrections.caveats: Rust-only format, not wire-compatible or cross-language like protobuf. The baselines are Rust protobuf crates (prost 0.14.4; Google's protobuf 4.36.1 Rust crate is also on the page and is usually slower than prost), not C++ libprotobuf. The claim's log ratio uses prost 'populate + encode'; against plain encode the gain is ~4.7x. The mesh result (~6 MB in ~142 us, close to memcpy speed) comes from savefile bulk-copying POD arrays, so the 41-72x mesh gain does not carry over to other data. On string-heavy data (log, minecraft_savedata) deserialize wins only ~1.6-1.7x.

notes: Every quoted number matches savefile's and prost's rows in the shootout README. I rewrote claimed_speedup to show encode-only and populate+encode side by side and to add the other two datasets, because the original picked the most favourable prost variant for the log dataset. Metadata checked with gh: MIT, 109 stars, not a fork, last commit 2026-07-13, active.

tier_reason: docs/BENCHMARKS.md compares noyalib directly against yaml-rust2 (and serde_yaml_ng, serde_yml, yaml-spanned, serde-saphyr). It states Apple M4, Rust 1.95 stable and --release with LTO=fat, codegen-units=1, panic=abort. The benchmark code is public at crates/noyalib/benches/comparison.rs (SIMD scan: benches/structural_bitmask.rs). First-party, but it meets the A bar.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Headline table (Apple M4, Rust 1.95, LTO=fat): deserialize to Value is 1.11x-1.36x faster than yaml-rust2 across 5 fixtures (k8s multi-doc 85.1 us at 1.11x, simple 1.40 us at 1.36x). Against the other Rust crates it is 1.38x-2.00x faster (serde_yaml_ng 1.42-1.84x, serde_yml 1.48-1.96x, yaml-spanned 1.38-1.74x, serde-saphyr 1.69-2.00x). Serialize is 3.00x-4.34x faster than serde_yaml_ng. The serde-saphyr head-to-head table (Apple A18 Pro, rustc 1.98.0, default bench profile) shows 1.21x-3.31x over yaml-rust2 and 2.55x-3.26x over serde-saphyr 1.2.0. The SIMD StructuralIter scan on 1 MiB is 4.2x (stable) / 9.2x (nightly-simd) faster than a memchr find_any_of loop.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Headline table: Rust 1.95 stable, criterion --release (LTO=fat, codegen-units=1, panic=abort), --warm-up-time 2 --measurement-time 4. serde-saphyr head-to-head table: rustc 1.98.0 (88d9e12ae 2026-08-18), default bench profile with no LTO tuning.

notes: The numbers match the page, except that the lower end of the range against the other crates is 1.38x (yaml-spanned, large_list), not 1.42x. The README says the crate is dual-licensed Apache-2.0 OR MIT (LICENSE-APACHE and LICENSE-MIT), but the GitHub API reports only Apache-2.0. The only baselines are pure-Rust YAML crates, and libyaml/yaml-cpp are never tested; the existing caveat already says so. Metadata checked with gh: 10 stars, not a fork, last commit 2026-09-22.
